stories.title: OpenAI's autonomous pipeline patches 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation bugs
stories.rationale: Concrete numbers, primary source, agentic security at scale — directly on-profile.
stories.summary: OpenAI built an autonomous pipeline that found, validated, and generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. The work was also highlighted in third-party AI news roundups covering kernel security.

stories.title: Inkling 2 Small: 594B MoE trained in 68 hours on 12T tokens
stories.rationale: Concrete training-efficiency numbers and model capabilities; on-profile research.
stories.summary: A new report details Inkling 2 Small, a 17A-594B mixture-of-experts model trained in 68 hours on 12T tokens, said to beat Muse Spark. Coverage also includes METR's study of AI research conducted at Anthropic.

stories.title: 'Weight-Space Programming': LLMs can natively read and write neural network weights
stories.rationale: Novel capabilities research with reproducibility on local models; relevant to capabilities readers.
stories.summary: A paper found that frontier models like GPT-6 Astra can interpret and modify the raw floating-point weights of neural networks described as text, with smaller models like Qwen 3.8 27B showing similar abilities. Follow-up work explores editing Qwen's weights to reduce reasoning loops and implications for recursive self-improvement.

stories.title: New agent benchmarks: BioBasicsBench, LifeVal, and CWE-bench v2
stories.rationale: Multiple concrete evals for agent capabilities including security; useful for evals-focused reader.
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark for how AI agents interpret raw wet-lab experimental data, and LifeVal, which measures how well AI helps complete everyday tasks. Hugging Face separately released CWE-bench v2, expanding coverage and transparency for vulnerability-detection evaluation.

stories.title: Google ships Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash as NVIDIA releases Cosmos 3 world models
stories.rationale: Two primary-source model releases spanning multimodal and world simulation.
stories.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a faster, cost-effective multimodal model supporting longer clips. NVIDIA published new Cosmos 3 open models for interactive world simulation.

stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber and Daybreak Red for aligned cybersecurity agents
stories.rationale: Major model release for security agents, now deployable via AWS GovCloud; primary source.
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model for finding exploitable vulnerabilities and developing fixes within authorized scope. The related Daybreak Red is now available to approved customers in AWS GovCloud (US-East) through Amazon Bedrock.

stories.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre, builds Pando Git backend to scale Codex-era development
stories.rationale: Codex tooling acquisition plus novel dev infra; directly relevant to agentic SDLC.
stories.summary: OpenAI announced it will acquire Pierre Computer Company to expand Codex's tools for building, understanding, and reviewing code. It also detailed Pando, a Git-compatible backend designed for the scale of development that Codex enables.

stories.title: Legora builds legal agents without access to client data traces
stories.rationale: Real agentic deployment with a concrete eval-without-traces constraint; on-profile.
stories.summary: Legora's CTO describes building and testing legal agents when the firm cannot read any trace of agent activity because data belongs to client law firms. The discussion covers evals without traces, million-cell tabular review, and pressure on the billable-hour model.

stories.title: Re-examining U.S. Census data on corporate AI adoption
stories.rationale: Concrete data analysis of real enterprise adoption trends; aligns with adoption interest.
stories.summary: Simon Willison revisited Census Bureau data previously cited to show slowing U.S. corporate AI adoption and re-ran the numbers a year later. The post analyzes what changed and cautions about interpreting the figures.

stories.title: Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' exposed passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files
stories.rationale: Concrete coding-agent security failure with hard numbers; highly relevant to dev tooling readers.
stories.summary: Security firm Apiiro reported that Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' permission feature led to secrets being leaked across 1,122 public GitHub files. The finding highlights risks in coding-agent permission models and autonomous commits.
